capture_method: Genuine browser interface screenshots captured through the live Lab10 and Lab11 controls; no mock interface or fabricated results. Frames switch at the matching spoken sentences. Inputs and restored recalculations were verified.

scenes.label: Select the gas-solid experiment
scenes.sentence_prefix: We are now in the real Lab ten interface.

scenes.label: Enter volume, inventory and temperature
scenes.sentence_prefix: Enter a temperature of three hundred kelvin and a free gas volume of one liter.

scenes.label: Enter the sublimation correlation and calculate
scenes.sentence_prefix: The reference temperature is also three hundred kelvin.

scenes.label: Read case 10A and close the volatile balance
scenes.sentence_prefix: The result for case ten A is solid plus gas.

scenes.label: Interpret the temperature sweep
scenes.sentence_prefix: Change the View menu to Gas and solid amounts.

scenes.label: Reduce the inventory below the saturation capacity
scenes.sentence_prefix: Now change only the total volatile inventory to zero point zero zero two mole and calculate again.

scenes.label: Add an ideal inert gas at fixed temperature and volume
scenes.sentence_prefix: For case ten C, keep the volatile inventory at zero point zero zero two mole and add zero point zero zero two mole of inert gas.

scenes.label: Interpret partial, total and sublimation pressure
scenes.sentence_prefix: In the pressure view, distinguish the three curves using their legend labels.

scenes.label: Name and retain the three calculated cases
scenes.sentence_prefix: Keep a separate record for each calculated case.

scenes.label: Download all three cases together
scenes.sentence_prefix: Select Download comparison to preserve all three cases in one file.

scenes.label: Choose the saved comparison JSON
scenes.sentence_prefix: We will now reopen the saved file from the beginning of the restore workflow.

scenes.label: Choose the imported case to restore
scenes.sentence_prefix: The three case labels have returned after loading the comparison.

scenes.label: Verify the reopened calculation
scenes.sentence_prefix: The recalculated case again reports solid plus gas, a volatile partial pressure of ten kilopascals, and the same gas and solid amounts as our original record.

scenes.label: Open the adsorption model comparison
scenes.sentence_prefix: We are now in the real Lab eleven interface.

scenes.label: Set the Langmuir parameters and units
scenes.sentence_prefix: Select Langmuir and check a capacity of two moles per kilogram and an affinity of zero point one per kilopascal.

scenes.label: Enter the closed-vessel inventory
scenes.sentence_prefix: Expand Closed vessel, fixed temperature and free gas volume.

scenes.label: Check the first Langmuir vessel balance
scenes.sentence_prefix: For case eleven A, the equilibrium adsorbate partial pressure is about six point zero eight zero kilopascals.

scenes.label: Match the Henry slope
scenes.sentence_prefix: Before changing the model, save the calculated Langmuir case with its interpretation and label.

scenes.label: Compare Henry and Langmuir at the same inventory
scenes.sentence_prefix: The Henry calculation gives about four point one six five kilopascals for case eleven B.

scenes.label: Double the adsorbent mass while retaining the Langmuir model
scenes.sentence_prefix: For case eleven C, return the selected model to Langmuir and increase the dry adsorbent mass from ten to twenty grams.

scenes.label: Distinguish specific uptake from total adsorbed amount
scenes.sentence_prefix: With twenty grams of adsorbent, the Langmuir pressure falls to about two point eight four five kilopascals.

scenes.label: Compare model domains on a wider chart
scenes.sentence_prefix: Save the third case, then widen the maximum chart pressure to one hundred kilopascals and calculate again to inspect the model shapes.

scenes.label: Retain the three adsorption studies
scenes.sentence_prefix: The Study workspace now contains three named model studies: Langmuir with ten grams, Henry with ten grams, and Langmuir with twenty grams.

scenes.label: Download the adsorption comparison
scenes.sentence_prefix: Select Download comparison to save these three model studies together.

scenes.label: Reopen the saved adsorption comparison
scenes.sentence_prefix: To check that the study is reusable, clear the temporary comparison only after saving the file.

scenes.label: Restore the original Langmuir case
scenes.sentence_prefix: After import, select Restore beside case eleven A, Langmuir ten grams.

scenes.label: Verify the reopened balance and return to the worksheet
scenes.sentence_prefix: The restored and recalculated Langmuir case again gives approximately six point zero eight zero kilopascals and the same gas and adsorbed amounts as before.
